comments.author: @karinanalbandyan3009
comments.text: I would like to stay at one of those stations over winter. I would actually enjoy that. I would enjoy the isolation. I’m already living a life of isolation, but of course not to that degree. I don’t mind the isolation at all. In fact, it would be quite exciting for me to be in a place so very different where it’s always dark and cold. I find it comforting, living on the edge of the world in company of just a few. Especially when it comes with such comforts as electricity/warmth, and good food. It would be like a vacation of hibernation for me.  I can only imagine how incredible the night sky looks from that location. In reality, though, I’m probably imagining something very different from the actual conditions at those Antarctica stations. Probably my fantasy does not match the reality of what goes on there. In my mind, I’m imagining like a resort but in reality, it’s probably more like survival situation 24 seven.

replies.text: Yeah I'm the same as a composer I can't quite have enough solitude

replies.author: @karinanalbandyan3009
replies.text: @Whe@WhereonEarth4Kolation would not drive me crazy or make me depressed. I have never experienced depression in my life, although I have gone through some violent traumatic things in my childhood, and my x marriage. Being kind and respectful to others comes naturally to me, but I’m no pushover though. I stick up for myself and others. I find it fascinating being so far from everyone  existing in this lonely icy world. If they could somehow make this place warm and make sure that crew members have really yummy foods available to them throughout the whole stay, in that environment, I can actually thrive there. I don’t have any specific qualifications. I’m not a scientist or a biologist, but I do know how to cook and bake really well. Cooks who know how to prepare meals that uplift you body, mind and spirit, could be very valuable at that place, because during the video the guy did say that good food is necessary for the morale of the crew. If anything I can make meals that deliver great joy and comfort. So yeah, I could be a cook there if they even have this position..

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That instinct toward the isolation rather than away from it is exactly what draws the people who actually do winter over there - and you're right that the reality leans more survival-logistics than resort, though the night sky part of your imagination is probably spot on. Few things compare to an Antarctic sky with zero light pollution for hundreds of miles.

comments.text: The psychological symptoms sound very similar to those reported by inmates in long-term solitary confinement. Very interesting.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That's a striking comparison, and not without basis - isolation research does draw real parallels between extreme remote environments and confinement settings, since the underlying stressors (limited social contact, monotony, sensory deprivation) overlap quite a bit.
